subject: exercise-sports-science
title: Energy Systems: Three Systems Sharing One Bout Exit Ticket

questions.prompt: A student says the body uses only one energy system at a time and switches cleanly to the next one when the first runs out. What is the best correction?

choices.text: The student is right - each system works alone in turn

All three systems are active from the first second and overlap throughout the bout; only the largest contributor changes as the bout continues - ATP-PC fades as the phosphocreatine store drains, anaerobic glycolysis peaks as lactate builds, and the aerobic system rises to dominate longer work.
Only the aerobic system matters, because it supplies 75 percent in longer work
ATP-PC never fades, because the phosphocreatine store refills instantly

questions.misconception: The body uses only one energy system at a time and switches cleanly to the next one when the first runs out.
questions.feedback: If you agreed with the student, that is the trap: The body uses only one energy system at a time and switches cleanly to the next one when the first runs out. Reteach point: All three systems are active from the first second and overlap throughout the bout; only the largest contributor changes as the bout continues - ATP-PC fades as the phosphocreatine store drains, anaerobic glycolysis peaks as lactate builds, and the aerobic system rises to dominate longer work.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain why there is no clean switch at about 10 seconds.
questions.answer: At about 10 seconds ATP-PC has faded to 35 percent as the phosphocreatine store drains, but glycolysis is already supplying 40 percent and the aerobic system 25 percent, so the systems overlap rather than switch.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names all three shares at 10 seconds: no share is 100 percent and none is zero, so nothing has switched on or off.

questions.prompt: Minutes into the bout, which statement is correct?

choices.text: The aerobic system supplies 100 percent and the other two have switched off
The aerobic system supplies 75 percent, while glycolysis still supplies 20 percent and ATP-PC 5 percent
Glycolysis supplies 75 percent as lactate builds
ATP-PC is back to 70 percent because its store has refilled

questions.feedback: Scene 4 shows the aerobic system dominating at 75 percent in longer work, but glycolysis at 20 percent and ATP-PC at 5 percent are still contributing.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state which system holds the largest share at about 30 seconds and what builds up as it works.
questions.answer: At about 30 seconds anaerobic glycolysis holds the largest share at 55 percent, and lactate builds as it works.
questions.feedback: A strong answer pairs the largest share with its marker: glycolysis at 55 percent, with lactate building.
